description: LearnLite initial verification set (E1-E5), v0. source_id values follow the agreed source list (LearnLite_Module1_Sources.xlsx). source_text values are still short placeholder paraphrases written for testing; replace each with the exact excerpt from its source before reporting results.

items.statement: A chatbot writes its answer by predicting one token at a time.
items.source_text: Large language models generate text one token at a time. At each step the model predicts the most likely next token based on the tokens that came before it, then repeats the process until the answer is complete.

items.statement: A chatbot looks up every answer on the internet before replying.
items.source_text: Most language models answer from patterns learned during training and do not search the internet by default. Some chatbot products add a separate web-search tool, but only when that feature is switched on.
items.why: Over-generalises; the source says most models do not search by default.

items.statement: AI never makes mistakes if you ask clearly.
items.source_text: Clear prompts that give context, a role, the task and the desired format usually lead to more useful answers. However, even with a good prompt, language models can still produce incorrect or made-up information.

items.statement: A higher temperature makes the AI's answers more varied.
items.source_text: Temperature is a setting that controls randomness in word choice. A low temperature makes answers more predictable and repetitive; a higher temperature makes answers more varied and creative, but also more likely to drift off topic.

items.statement: AI hallucinations only happen with hard questions.
items.source_text: A hallucination is when a language model states false or made-up information as if it were true. Hallucinations are more common on obscure or complex questions, but they can happen on any topic, including simple ones, and are often stated confidently.
items.why: Hard questions raise the risk, but 'only' is too narrow.
